*Me thinking about this year, sitting on the stoop with my tea:*

I'm 65 now, been farming this same ground for 40 years. My wife and me are the main workers. Two of my sons work in the city — they send a little money home, which helps with fertilizer — and my daughter-in-law and the grandkids pitch in when school's out and at harvest. That's seven mouths total, but only two real pairs of hands most days.

My 20.4 mu — the main piece, about 18 mu of decent ground, I do wheat-maize like everybody in the village. The other 2 mu or so, on the edge where the soil's poorer, I keep in millet for the family. My wife makes porridge from it and we sell a little at the market in town. We've always kept millet, it's the old way.

Right now it's already late April. My wheat has been in the ground since last October — I planted around the 10th like usual, Jimai 22 seed from the same dealer my neighbor Old Wang uses. I already put one bag of compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, per mu before planting back in the fall, and in March when the wheat started standing up I topdressed about half a bag of urea per mu. That's what my father taught me and what Old Wang still does. So for the wheat this year, what's left is one more watering at grain filling if it doesn't rain, and then the combine in early June. I'll watch for aphids — if I see them I'll spray once, but if not I save the money. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu. Expecting about the same, maybe 430 if the weather holds.

Right after the combine takes the wheat, middle of June, the maize goes in. It's a tight turnaround, just a day or two. I hire the seed drill — don't own one, wouldn't pay for myself. Hybrid seed, Xianyu 335 or whatever's stocked. I spread urea at planting, about 30 kg per mu, and a little compound. No topdress. If the summer rains come, I don't water at all. If it's a dry year like two years back, I'll give it one watering. One spray of herbicide after planting for the weeds. Last year maize was 480 per mu, year before was better.

The millet goes in next month, late May. I saved seed from last year's crop — no point buying. Plant it by hand with my wife, put a little compound at planting, that's it. Millet doesn't need much water, that's why I put it on the poor ground. Harvest in late September by hand, beat it out on a tarp. Maybe 250 kg per mu, not much, but it's for us.

Money is tight but the boys help. I figure about 12,000 or 13,000 yuan total for inputs this year — compound fertilizer is the biggest bite, urea second, then the custom drill and combine. I don't spend on pesticide unless I actually see a problem. No sense throwing money at what isn't there.
